query: Earlier W-based high-entropy alloys showed promising microstructural stability, high-temperature strength, and irradiation tolerance, but most contained Nb, Mo, Cr, or Ni, whose activation behavior and other service limitations restrict their suitability for plasma-facing components. Candidate structural materials must combine thermal and mechanical performance with low neutron activation and rapid radioactive decay. The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy uses refractory, relatively low-activation constituents and has shown creep and molten-salt-corrosion resistance, yet its plastic strain and toughness remain unreported and poorly understood. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains what governs its plastic strain and toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing-component service? Specify a controlled comparison that would isolate the hypothesized cause, the observations predicted relative to pure tungsten, the boundaries of validity, the cited prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The improved plastic strain and toughness of the equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy relative to pure tungsten are governed by the solid-solution strengthening and grain boundary cohesion provided by the multi-principal-element alloying, which enhances dislocation glide and reduces grain boundary embrittlement.
generation.intervention: Controlled comparison of high-temperature tensile tests and Charpy impact tests
generation.conditions: Tests conducted at 500°C, 700°C, and 900°C, with strain rates of 10^-3 s^-1 and 10^-1 s^-1
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundary cohesion and dislocation glide
generation.mechanism: Solid-solution strengthening and grain boundary cohesion provided by the multi-principal-element alloying
generation.predicted_outcome: The alloy is expected to exhibit higher plastic strain and toughness than pure tungsten at all temperatures and strain rates, with a more pronounced difference at higher temperatures and lower strain rates
generation.boundary: The results are expected to be valid for the equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy under high-temperature plasma-facing-component service conditions
generation.uncertainty: The results may not be able to isolate the effects of solid-solution strengthening and grain boundary cohesion, and additional tests or characterization techniques may be needed to provide a more complete understanding of the underlying mechanisms

falsification_experiment.design: High-temperature tensile tests and Charpy impact tests on the equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy and pure tungsten, with additional characterization techniques to evaluate the effects of solid-solution strengthening and grain boundary cohesion
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the results show no significant difference in plastic strain and toughness between the equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy and pure tungsten, or if the additional characterization techniques do not support the expected effects of solid-solution strengthening and grain boundary cohesion, the hypothesis would be falsified
